Living with Purpose—Discovering Your Calling.
You know, searching for purpose is just something we all do. At some point, every teen wonders—does my life really matter? Is there something special out there for me? The thing is, when you look at the Bible, stories about calling aren’t about fame or fortune. They’re actually about everyday people being invited into something much bigger than themselves.
Imagine a student who loves music. Maybe she’s asking herself, does my passion really count? Then she reads about David, who played his harp for a troubled king. David’s music didn’t change the world overnight, but it brought comfort and peace right when it was needed most. Suddenly, it clicks—purpose isn’t always about huge achievements. Sometimes it’s just about using what you have, exactly where you are.
Or think about a boy who feels invisible. He wonders if he’ll ever do something that matters. But then, he hears the story of the boy with five loaves and two fish—who offers his small lunch to Jesus. The real miracle isn’t just the food, but the willingness to give what little he has. Most of us don’t realize how much small acts can mean, but these stories remind us—nothing offered in love is ever wasted.
There’s also that teen who loves science, but feels torn—can you have faith and curiosity at the same time? She finds her answer in the story of Solomon, who asks God for wisdom and then explores the world. The Bible’s idea of purpose isn’t about shutting down your questions. It’s about letting your curiosity and your faith work together.
And sometimes, purpose shows up in the places you’d least expect. Maybe there’s a student who’s battled anxiety, and now realizes her own struggles help her support others who are fighting the same battle. The story of Paul, who turns his pain into encouragement for others, shows us that even our toughest moments can play a part in a bigger story.
Over time, you start to see—calling isn’t about waiting for a lightning bolt. It’s about paying attention to the needs around you, the gifts you’ve been given, and those quiet nudges you can’t ignore. The wisdom from the Bible is simple: start right where you are, use what you have, and trust that your life matters more than you know.
